content.title: About
content.content: French toast is a dish made from bread slices soaked in a mixture of eggs, milk, sugar and spices, then fried on a pan until golden. It is traditionally served with syrup, berries, fruit or a dusting of powdered sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in France in the 17th century and was originally called "pain perdu" – "lost bread".
French toast is often used as a way to rescue stale bread, turning it into a tasty and nutritious meal.
In the United States its popularity surged in the mid‑20th century with the introduction of ready‑made batter mixes.
There are many variations: with cinnamon, vanilla, rum, orange zest or even cheese.
In some countries, such as Japan, French toast is served with soy sauce and mayonnaise.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Eggs and milk in the batter provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2 and B6 vitamins from eggs and bread support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Milk adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Improves iron absorption
items.content: Vitamin C from accompanying berries or fruit enhances iron uptake from the bread.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates in the bread provide fast‑acting energy, making it a popular breakfast.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Frequent consumption with generous amounts of syrup or sugar can contribute to weight gain and blood glucose spikes.

items.title: Egg or milk allergy
items.content: People with food allergies may react to these ingredients.

items.title: Trans‑fat formation during frying
items.content: Using oils heated to high temperatures can generate trans fats.

items.title: Gluten for sensitive individuals
items.content: Traditional bread contains gluten, so those with celiac disease should use a gluten‑free alternative.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beat eggs with milk, add a pinch of salt, sugar and spices (cinnamon, vanilla). Dip bread slices in the mixture, let them soak, then fry in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat until golden on both sides. Serve hot with maple syrup, berries, fruit or a dusting of powdered sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared French toast is best enjoyed immediately. Leftovers can be cooled, placed in an airtight container and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in an oven or toaster to restore a crisp crust.
